description: I1 SAML cert substitution: with CA-based signature validation configured, attacker-signed SAMLResponse should be rejected.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify SAMLResponse signatures against the configured CA trust anchor; it must not accept attacker-signed assertions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP accepted attacker-signed SAMLResponse despite CA-based signature validation being configured (trust anchor substitution / missing signature verification).

description: I1 SAML issuer mismatch: with ssoIssuer pinned, a forged Issuer should be rejected even if signature checks are otherwise configured.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured IdP issuer (ssoIssuer) and reject assertions with an untrusted Issuer value.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute issuer-mismatch outcome to issuer validation (possible connector/SP-initiated flow misconfiguration).
SP accepted SAML assertion with forged/untrusted Issuer despite ssoIssuer being pinned (issuer validation bypass).

description: I1 insecure configuration regression check: toggle insecureSkipSignatureValidation from true to false and ensure attacker-signed assertions stop working (verification policy must match consumption).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: When signature validation is enabled (insecureSkipSignatureValidation=false with CA configured), Dex must not accept attacker-signed SAML assertions that were previously accepted under insecure mode.

oracle_checks.violation_description: In insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true mode, attacker-signed SAMLResponse was unexpectedly rejected; cannot validate the regression/toggle behavior.
After switching to signature validation (insecureSkipSignatureValidation=false with CA), SP still accepted attacker-signed SAMLResponse (verification policy not applied to consumed proof).

description: I1: Attempt to bypass proof integrity by omitting SAML Conditions (semantic proof changes) while keeping a signed-looking response; SP should reject assertions missing Conditions.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the exact semantic proof it consumes; an assertion missing Conditions must not be accepted as equivalent to a valid assertion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to Conditions mutation vs misconfiguration.
Dex accepted a SAML assertion with Conditions omitted; verification policy did not enforce semantic proof integrity.

description: I1 attack: Attempt to splice a SAMLResponse for one principal into another SP-initiated flow by swapping relay_state, probing whether Dex verifies the proof against the correct request context (InResponseTo/state binding).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify that the SAMLResponse it consumes is the same proof it verified for the specific SP-initiated request context; relay_state/state splicing must not allow a proof for principal A to be consumed in principal B's flow.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login for flow A failed; cannot interpret splice attempt outcome.
Dex accepted a SAMLResponse for principal A when posted with flow B relay_state; indicates proof verification may not be bound to the consumed request context (semantic proof mismatch).

description: Replay the exact same SAML assertion containing <OneTimeUse/> twice; second attempt must be rejected if OneTimeUse is enforced.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse must not be accepted more than once (anti-replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion that included <OneTimeUse/>, indicating OneTimeUse anti-replay is not enforced.

description: Expired assertion acceptance and replay: first attempt uses an expired assertion; second attempt replays the exact same expired assertion ID to test both expiry enforcement and replay rejection.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired SAML assertions must be rejected, and an assertion (even if expired) must not be accepted more than once.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; expired-assertion results are inconclusive due to possible connector/flow misconfiguration.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); assertion lifetime is not enforced.
Dex accepted a replay of the same expired SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID); anti-replay is missing or scoped incorrectly.

description: OneTimeUse replay after revocation: perform a successful OneTimeUse login, revoke the resulting session, then attempt to reuse the same OneTimeUse assertion ID in a new SP flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OneTimeUse assertions must be single-use regardless of downstream session revocation; revoking the session must not reset upstream assertion replay protection.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control OneTimeUse SAML login failed; replay results are inconclusive.
Dex accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion after session revocation; OneTimeUse or replay cache is not enforced correctly.

description: I2: Use a OneTimeUse assertion successfully, revoke the resulting session, then attempt to reuse the same OneTimeUse assertion ID in a new SP-initiated flow; second must still be rejected (revocation must not reset anti-replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: OneTimeUse and assertion-ID replay protections must persist independently of session revocation; revoking a session must not allow reusing the same one-time SAML artifact.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Initial OneTimeUse login failed; cannot evaluate replay-after-revocation behavior
SP accepted a replayed OneTimeUse SAML assertion after session revocation — anti-replay state not persisted correctly

description: Replay the same OAuth2 authorization code twice after a SAML upstream login; second exchange must be rejected (auth code is one-time). Uses two identities to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts; exchanging the same code twice must fail even if the upstream SAML login succeeded.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (second /token exchange succeeded) — auth code replay not prevented
Control exchange failed; cannot distinguish replay protection from broken auth flow

description: Cross-session SAML callback splicing: initiate two SP flows (A and B) then post a SAMLResponse bound to flow A while using relay_state from flow B; must be rejected if flow is coherently bound to session/state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must bind the SAMLResponse (InResponseTo/relay context) to the correct SP-initiated session; cross-session splicing of relay_state must not authenticate.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse with relay_state from a different SP-initiated flow (cross-session splicing), indicating broken flow coherence.

description: Connector confusion: start SP-initiated auth targeting SAML connector, then post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback path; must be rejected if callback is bound to the initiating connector.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback must be bound to the initiating connector/session; posting a response to the wrong connector_id callback must not complete authentication.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse posted to a different connector callback than the one used to initiate the flow, indicating connector/session confusion.

description: Step-skipping: attempt to POST a SAMLResponse to the callback without first initiating an SP flow; must be rejected (InResponseTo/state binding enforced).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must enforce order-preserving SP-initiated SAML flow; unsolicited/IdP-initiated SAMLResponses must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsolicited SAMLResponse without an SP-initiated flow, indicating step-skipping / missing InResponseTo-state binding.

description: Attempt to reuse the same RelayState/SAMLResponse pair twice (callback replay without re-initiating) to test whether Dex enforces single-use/atomic completion of the SAML callback step within a flow.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback step must be atomic and order-preserving; once a flow is completed, re-posting the same callback material must not create a second valid login/session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a second SAML callback POST using the same RelayState/SAMLResponse without re-initiating the flow, indicating non-atomic or replayable callback handling (flow coherence violation).

description: Initiate two SP flows with different client_id values, then attempt to complete the SAML callback for flow A using RelayState from flow B (client-binding splice).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML response must be bound to the initiating OAuth client/session; cross-client splicing of state/relay context must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAML callback where the RelayState belonged to a different OAuth client flow, indicating missing client/session binding (flow coherence violation).

description: Start an SP-initiated SAML flow, then change the connector configuration (issuer pin) mid-flight and attempt to complete the original flow with a response using the old issuer. The completion must be rejected if the flow is coherently bound to current connector policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authentication flow completion must be coherent with the current connector configuration; mid-flight config changes must not allow completing a flow under stale policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex completed a SAML flow using an issuer that is no longer allowed after a mid-flight connector config change, indicating stale-policy completion or non-atomic flow coherence.

description: Session lifecycle coherence: complete a SAML login, revoke the resulting session, then attempt to reuse the original flow context (RelayState) to authenticate again without re-initiating. Must be rejected if flow context is not tied to session revocation and remains single-use.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Revoking a session must not allow reusing an already-consumed SAML flow context; the callback step must remain single-use and order-preserving regardless of session lifecycle operations.

oracle_checks.violation_description: After revoking the session, the already-consumed SAML flow context (RelayState) was still accepted without re-initiating, indicating broken flow atomicity/order binding.

description: Cross-session splice at the OAuth boundary: initiate two SP-initiated SAML flows, complete both, then attempt to exchange flow-A's auth code while presenting flow-B's redirect_uri. If Dex fails to bind code to the original request context, the exchange may succeed (flow coherence violation).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code exchange must be bound to the initiating authorization request context (client_id/redirect_uri/session). A code minted for one SP-initiated SAML flow must not be redeemable under a different flow's redirect_uri.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code minted for one SP-initiated SAML flow was redeemable with a different redirect_uri, indicating weak binding between auth request context and token exchange (flow coherence violation).
Control token exchange failed; cannot distinguish flow-coherence enforcement from generic SAML/OIDC misconfiguration.

description: Case confusion in SAML NameID: 'Admin' vs 'admin' should map to distinct downstream subjects; detect unintended case-folding collision.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals (NameID differing only by case) must not collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-folding collision: NameID 'Admin' and 'admin' mapped to the same downstream identity

description: I4 cross-protocol identity merge: compare a password-grant identity vs a SAML identity that uses the same email but a different NameID; ensure they do not collapse into one downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A local/password principal and a SAML principal with the same email but different unique identifier must not map to the same downstream subject unless explicitly linked by policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
SAML principal with same email as password user collapsed into the password user's downstream subject (account linking/merge without explicit binding)

description: I4 attack: SAML NameID homoglyph collision (Latin 'a' vs Cyrillic 'а') should not collapse into the same downstream subject if Dex preserves exact NameID bytes/semantics.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream SAML principals with visually similar but different Unicode codepoints in NameID must map to different downstream identities (no homoglyph-based principal collision).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Homoglyph-distinct SAML NameID values collapsed into the same downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: I5 attack: SAML assertion missing <Conditions> (no audience/time bounds) should be rejected; if accepted, broker may grant permissions without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must not exceed UpstreamIntent(auth_context) ∩ BrokerPolicy(config); an assertion without Conditions has no upstream-scoped audience/time intent and must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute subsequent acceptance/rejection to Conditions enforcement.
SP accepted SAML assertion without Conditions (no audience/time bounds), enabling permissions without upstream intent constraints.

description: I5 attack: If allowedGroups is configured, authentication should be denied unless the user is in an allowed group. Probe for delimiter/parsing confusion where a single group string could be split to include an allowed group unexpectedly.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: BrokerPolicy(config) group gating must be enforced exactly; malformed/ambiguous group strings must not be parsed to satisfy allowedGroups unintentionally.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed under allowedGroups gating; cannot interpret group parsing bypass attempt.
User without intended allowed group was authenticated (potential group parsing/delimiter confusion), violating BrokerPolicy(config) authorization binding.

description: SAML connector with allowedGroups + filterGroups=true: attacker presents assertion with both allowed and extra privileged groups; verify whether Dex leaks extra groups/permissions beyond BrokerPolicy filtering intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: When BrokerPolicy(config) uses allowedGroups with filterGroups=true, effective permissions/claims must not include groups outside allowedGroups even if upstream assertion includes them.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_attacker_groups_http_status == 200 AND user_attacker_groups_meta contains "users" AND user_attacker_groups_meta not in "admins"
oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex emitted/retained non-allowed group ('admins') despite filterGroups=true, enabling permissions beyond BrokerPolicy(config).

description: Config change + re-auth: enable insecureSkipSignatureValidation then attempt attacker-signed SAML assertion; verify that acceptance is configuration-driven and should be treated as an authorization-binding risk if enabled unintentionally.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: BrokerPolicy(config) must not allow effective permissions from untrusted upstream assertions; if signature validation is disabled, attacker can assert arbitrary groups/identity and exceed intended authorization.

oracle_checks.violation_description: With signature validation enabled (CA configured), Dex accepted attacker-signed assertion, allowing permissions beyond upstream intent.
Dex accepted attacker-signed assertion when insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true; this permits arbitrary group/identity injection and breaks authorization binding if enabled unintentionally.
